root_cause.text: `loongson_gpu_fixup_dma_hang()` in `arch/loongarch/pci/pci.c` assumed the PCI device ID switch would always match a valid LS2K/LS7A display controller and then dereferenced `crtc_reg`, but on systems with a discrete GPU the derived device can be an unexpected function so the switch falls through with an uninitialized/random MMIO base, causing an ADE on `readl()`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE text says “The switch case in loongson_gpu_fixup_dma_hang() may not DC2 or DC3, and readl(crtc_reg) will access with random address, because the ‘device’ is from ‘base+PCI_DEVICE_ID’, ‘base’ is from ‘pdev->devfn+1’,” and the patch adds `default: iounmap(regbase); return;` before the `for (i = 0; i < CRTC_NUM_MAX; i++, crtc_reg += crtc_offset)` loop, showing the bug was unchecked handling of an unexpected switch value leading to invalid MMIO access.

bic_trace_step.reason:
The vulnerable construct is present in this function body. `loongson_gpu_fixup_dma_hang()` derives `device = readw(base + PCI_DEVICE_ID);` and then only initializes `crtc_reg`/`crtc_offset` in the switch for `PCI_DEVICE_ID_LOONGSON_DC2` and `PCI_DEVICE_ID_LOONGSON_DC3`:

- `switch (device) { case PCI_DEVICE_ID_LOONGSON_DC2: crtc_reg = regbase + 0x1240; crtc_offset = 0x10; break; case PCI_DEVICE_ID_LOONGSON_DC3: crtc_reg = regbase; crtc_offset = 0x400; break; }`

There is no `default:` or error return. The code then immediately dereferences `crtc_reg` in `for (i = 0; i < CRTC_NUM_MAX; i++, crtc_reg += crtc_offset) { val = readl(crtc_reg); ... }`. This matches the root cause: if the derived device is not one of the expected display controllers, the switch falls through with an uninitialized `crtc_reg`, leading to an invalid `readl()` access. The fix is not present because there is no validation/guard against unexpected device IDs before using `crtc_reg`.
